title: Contextual Probe Orchestrator and Hypothesis-Driven Canary Fences
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Implement a Contextual Probe Orchestrator (CPO) to improve regression detection during staged model flips. The CPO combines stratified live sampling, synthetic perturbation injection, and hypothesis-driven fences to reduce false positives/negatives in automatic rollback decisions. Scope: - Probe bucketization by customer cohort, request size, prompt template family, and recency bucket. - Synthetic perturbation matrix to exercise edge behaviors deterministically (format noise, length extremes, tiled stop sequences). - Per-cohort baseline scorecards computed from rolling windows and bootstrapped confidence intervals. - Hypothesis-driven canary fences: gating rules expressed as statistical hypotheses (e.g., delta > X and bootstrap p < Y) with hysteresis windows to avoid flapping. Acceptance criteria: 1) Offline simulation shows reduction in false rollback triggers vs current heuristic by >= 30% on historical rollouts. 2) Live shadow sweep runs for 48h with <1% false positive rollback alerts when using CPO signals. 3) Automated gating config UI in the Console exposes per-cohort thresholds and an opt-in toggle. Out of scope: major changes to KV cache or kernel scheduling.
gating_logic: Primary gate: (scorecard_mean_delta >= 1.8) AND (bootstrap_p_value <= 0.01) measured over a 30-minute sliding window
Secondary gate: cohort_regression_rate >= 0.015 for two consecutive 10-minute windows triggers alert but requires human confirm for rollback
Hysteresis: require 3 successive failing windows OR persistent delta for 60 minutes before initiating automatic rollback
Fallback: if latency p99 increases > 2x OR error rate > 0.5% across global traffic, immediate scaledown to previous model variant
test_plan: Offline: run historical-sim harness (conftest: rollout-sim-v2) comparing baseline heuristic vs CPO on 12 months of canary data
Shadow sweep: route 100% shadow traffic for 48h with CPO generating alerts but no automated rollback
Staged canary: 5% -> 25% -> 50% ramps with CPO gates enforced and automatic rollback enabled only after opt-in; first run will use human-in-loop for final rollback decision
A/B experiment: run paired A/B for 7 days to validate user-facing metric impact and false positive rate
implementation_notes: Introduce probe bucketing service in inference-router to tag requests with cohort metadata
Lightweight synthetic probe engine lives in eval-harness; probes are stored as signed fixtures to ensure reproducibility
Use existing metric pipeline (Prometheus + Mimir) and add a bootstrapping worker for p-value estimation that writes per-cohort summaries to metrics-store
Keep rollout decision workflow in rollout-orchestrator; add new decision hook that consumes CPO signals as input to existing canary state machine
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: overfitting probe sets to historical regressions -> Mitigation: rotate and expand synthetic perturbations monthly via auto-generation job
Risk: increased metric compute cost (bootstrap) -> Mitigation: sample cohorts adaptively and fall back to less-expensive t-test when sample size large
Risk: noisy per-customer baselines causing spurious human alerts -> Mitigation: require cohort-level min traffic threshold and blend global baseline when traffic low
deployment_plan: Feature flag gating for CPO and per-team opt-in in Console
Canary the orchestrator itself on internal clusters (dev->staging->prod) with synthetic-only traffic first
Enable live shadowing for 7 internal customers and monitor false positive rates before broader rollout
metrics_and_slo_targets: False rollback trigger rate <= 0.5% during shadow runs
Detection lead time: median time to detect real regression <= 12 minutes
Precision of automatic rollback decisions >= 95% on validated regressions
Additional metric cost budget: < 10% increase in metrics compute month-over-month for rollout telemetry
